Normalize the trailing feature dimensions of each sample.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | [Normalization](../categories/normalization.md) |
| Status | Runs |
| Search words | layernorm, normalization, transformer |

## Inputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Input** | Tensor | Yes | 1 | Feature or sequence activations to normalize. |

## Outputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Output** | Tensor | Yes | 1 | Normalized tensor with the same shape. |

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normalization | Normalized Shape | `normalized_shape` | Text | (empty) |   | The run | Comma-separated trailing dimensions; empty uses the current feature width. |
| Normalization | Epsilon | `eps` | Number | `1e-5` | `0.000000001-3.402823e38` | The run | Positive numerical stability term. Required. |
| Normalization | Elementwise Affine | `elementwise_affine` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Learn per-element scale and bias. Advanced. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Training (the compiled model) | Yes, as a layer of the model: compiled as a trainable CPU-backed transformer normalization layer |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.

## Usage

```text
Normalizes each sample independently.
```

## Tips

- Use in Transformers and RNNs.
- Works with batch size 1 unlike BatchNorm.
